title: A Dallas radio broadcast and gigs with a local band
summary: He played and sang 'Sleepy Time Down South' on a live radio broadcast with a Dallas band he cannot name, then did many gigs with them before graduating in 1932.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And, like, this band, I wish I could think of it, in Dallas that I made the radio program. The first thing, "Sleepy Time Down South." My mother was listening to the radio --
Were you with it?
Yes, I played with the band.
No kidding.
And --
Was it a young band? I mean, it wasn't high school kids.
I was the youngest thing in there, I'll tell you that.
Oh. And you got a radio -- you got an air shot.
Right, right.
From what, a dance hall?
WRR -- No, this is a radio station.
You went up there?
Yes.
To do a live broadcast.
To do a live broadcast. And I sang "Sleepy Time Down South."
Oh, you sang?
Yes.
How did they know you could sing? Oh, because you were in the Glee Club.
Well, at rehearsal, you know, --
Oh, yeah.

-- someone -- he wanted someone to sing the number, so they asked me to sing it. So I knew it so I sang the number, see. But I'm telling you, that little mike liked to frighten me to death. I was standing there and my knees were shaking.
And, of course, you probably didn't know too well how to use the mike, how to stay away from it and come in on it.
No, I think that was one of those crystal mikes, anyway, so you had to be close to it.
Oh, yeah, yeah.
So I sang the song. That was a big thing for me.
Yeah, you mother was --
Oh, yeah, she loved it. I wish I could think of --
Yeah. Oh, that was very good. Well, did you work with them on and off?
I used to do a lot of gigs with them.
Oh, you did?
Yeah.
So this was really your first introduction to professional.
Well, really, yeah.
Funny that you can't put a name to them. You may, before we get through today.
I'm trying, I'm trying my best to think of it.
Yeah, well, we may find it in there somewhere. Do you remember any of the guys in it? Were any of the guys guys that --
Truthfully, no, now.
Well, probably they didn't go on.
No, he lasted just so long. It was one of those things.
Yeah.
He was a very good piano player.
But you were in school right then.
I was in school.
Yeah, yeah.
Right.
Yeah. Well, so, well, then, really, Gus, so you gigged with them at times. And you graduated in '32, did you say?
Right.
Right.
Well, did your mother want you to be something then? Did she want you to get a job doing something?
Oh, she always wanted me to stick with my music, you know.
Oh, she did.
Yeah, she knew that I loved it.
Yeah. Well, did you feel a need to gain some technical ability and technical facility on the drums, or did you not even feel the need because you were able to fulfill yourself?
